name: Crete
title: Holidays in Crete
intro: Pink sand beaches, a palace from the legend of the Minotaur and long sunny days. Here's what Crete is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and October are best, hot enough for the beach but kinder for exploring. July and August are very hot, windy and busy. Many resorts close from November to March.

things.name: Knossos
things.blurb: The palace of King Minos, where the Minotaur legend began. Go early before it gets hot.

things.name: Elafonissi
things.blurb: A lagoon with pink-tinged sand and shallow water, great for little ones.

things.name: Balos Lagoon
things.blurb: Turquoise water and white sand, easiest to reach by boat from Kissamos.

things.name: Chania old harbour
things.blurb: A Venetian harbour with a lighthouse, tavernas and an evening stroll.

things.name: CretAquarium
things.blurb: A good aquarium near Heraklion for a break from the sun.

things.name: Samaria Gorge
things.blurb: A 16 km hike down a dramatic gorge, for older children. Open roughly May to October.

faqs.question: Is Crete good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's big enough for beaches, history and mountains, and Greek tavernas are welcoming to children. You'll want a car to explore.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: A week covers one area well. Two weeks lets you see both the east and the west of the island.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: Where should we stay?
faqs.answer: Chania in the west has the best beaches and old town. The area around Heraklion and Hersonissos has big family resorts and water parks.
